business_scope.primary_industry_name: Rope-Access Structural Glass Replacement on Supertall Skyscrapers

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France's bilateral investment treaties and double taxation agreements apply according to the investor's or entity's residence and the relevant treaty text; treaty coverage must be verified for the specific investor and transaction.
Relevant EU instruments may include applicable EU trade agreements; France is not independently party to EU-level trade agreements.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French AML/CFT obligations are principally governed by Code monétaire et financier, including Articles L. 561-2 et seq. and L. 561-46 et seq., as amended. Beneficial-owner identification and filing are governed by Articles R. 561-1 et seq. and the applicable provisions of the Code de commerce. The filing is made through the national business-formalities one-stop shop and recorded in the Registre national des entreprises (RNE).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign company's certificate of incorporation or current registry extract, where a corporate shareholder is involved
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or public authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing state and document are covered by the Convention; otherwise consular legalization, subject to any applicable exemption

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation or filing, if executed outside France
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relevant signatory; notarization by a competent notary where required by the receiving authority or document form
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where applicable; otherwise consular legalization, subject to any applicable exemption

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity and address evidence for foreign individual directors, representatives, or beneficial owners, if requested by the filing authority, bank, or professional adviser
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent identity or address-document issuer in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication depends on document type, destination use, and applicable treaty; apostille or consular legalization may be required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Apply risk-based customer and beneficial-owner due diligence under the French Monetary and Financial Code. Identify domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, close associates, and family members; apply enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval where required. Screen against applicable EU and UN sanctions and French national measures. OFAC screening is not generally a standalone French statutory requirement but should be conducted where there is a US nexus, contractual requirement, or bank policy. Re-screen periodically and upon material ownership or control changes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); RNE records are accessible through the INPI portal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be declared in the incorporation documents and comply with French law and public order. French is customary for filings; foreign-language names are not generally prohibited. No general statutory transliteration rule applies. Check name availability against RNE and INPI trademark records; company-name availability does not establish trademark clearance.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying a regulated activity or status, including banking, insurance, investment services, and regulated professional titles, where use is restricted or could mislead the public
Terms implying a public authority, official endorsement, or protected institutional status without authorization
References to France or public institutions where their use is restricted or misleading
Names that are unlawful, contrary to public order, deceptive, or infringe prior company names, trade names, or trademarks
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no general company-name reservation procedure or fixed reservation validity period. If a filing is rejected, obtain the written decision and stated legal grounds, correct the name or supporting documents, and resubmit through the Guichet unique. Where legally available, challenge the decision through the competent administrative or judicial route identified in the decision and observe the stated time limit. A prior-right dispute may require proceedings before the competent court; an INPI trademark search is a separate clearance step.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SAS must declare a registered office (siège social). A domiciliation provider may be used if it is authorized and the applicable domiciliation rules and contract requirements are met. A virtual address alone may be inadequate for operational, banking, insurance, construction-safety, or customer due-diligence purposes. Rope-access facade work should maintain genuine operational arrangements, including appropriate records, personnel management, equipment and safety documentation, and a suitable correspondence and records address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No reliable statutory or official percentage is published for unannounced inspections. Construction-site and occupational-safety inspections may be conducted by competent authorities, including labour inspectors, according to risk and enforcement priorities; do not represent the likelihood as a quantified percentage.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Indicative professional-market estimate; official fees depend on the search requested

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting or review of SAS articles and incorporation documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; not a statutory tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Filing professional, if engaged; filing through the Guichet unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Indicative professional-market estimate; statutory filing charges, if any, are subject to current tariffs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (SAS regime), L.223-7 (domiciliation), L.123-1 et seq. (RCS registration); Decree n° 2023-393 of 24 May 2023 (Guichet Unique)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: INPI – Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises), operational portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; RCS extract issued by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) registration submitted exclusively via the Guichet Unique, attaching the executed articles of association (statuts), legal notice publication, and beneficial-owner declaration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum (share capital is freely fixed in the articles). Cash subscriptions must be paid up to at least 50% of nominal value at incorporation, the balance within five years; in-kind contributions are fully paid-up upon transfer. Funds must be deposited into a blocked French corporate bank account and may be withdrawn only after RCS registration is obtained.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION of FR_SAS (Société par Actions Simplifiée), dated 1 February 2026. The shareholders resolve: (1) APPROVAL of the articles of association containing the corporate purpose of rope-access structural glass replacement on supertall buildings; (2) SUBSCRIPTION of the share capital of EUR 1,000, consisting of 100 ordinary shares of EUR 10 par value, fully subscribed and paid up to the legal minimum in compliance with Article L.227-2 of the French Commercial Code; (3) ADOPTION of the registered office at [registered address in France]; (4) APPOINTMENT of [Name] as Président for an indefinite term with all powers permitted by law and the articles; (5) APPOINTMENT of [Name] as Director of Rope-Access Operations, subject to the Président's authority; (6) AUTHORIZATION of the Président to sign all incorporation filings, open the corporate bank account, and appoint the statutory auditor if thresholds are met; (7) RATIFICATION of compliance with anti-money-laundering and occupational-safety obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Clearance and Registered Office Domiciliation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI trademark and name search (data.inpi.fr) plus private domiciliation provider or commercial lease
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the availability of the desired corporate name against the RCS and trademarks, and secure a registered office address by lease, ownership deed, or domiciliation agreement with a certified third-party provider. No name reservation is mandatory, but obtaining a preliminary availability certificate avoids litigation risk.
required_dossiers: Copy of identity document of the founder(s)
Power of attorney if a third party files
Certified domiciliation agreement or lease deed
Name availability research report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered mark, select an alternative distinctive name or negotiate a coexistence agreement before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Notarization (if required) and Signature of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The founders or a legal counsel acting on their instructions; private deed is sufficient unless real estate is contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SAS articles including share capital, share classes, corporate purpose (ISIC 4390 rope-access façade works), management structure, decision-making rules, and share-transfer restrictions. Sign the articles in the number of counterparts required for the RCS filing and, if a civil-law notary is used, have the notary verify the identity and legal capacity of the signatories. If any contribution consists of real property, the articles must be executed as a notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (statuts)
Written decisions of the shareholder(s) approving the statutes
Statement of subscription and payment of the share capital
Valuation report (commissaire aux apports) for in-kind contributions exceeding EUR 30,000 unless waived by unanimous shareholders
Certificate of identity and good standing of the President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the statutes (e.g., incomplete clauses on share transfer or management powers), amend the articles by majority or unanimous resolution and re-submit the restated version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Account and Blocking of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank or credit institution with a physical or online presence in France
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate account in the name of the company in formation (using the draft articles or a 'dossier de constitution'), deposit the subscribed cash capital into a blocked account, and obtain the bank certificate (attestation de blocage) required for registration. The bank will perform KYC/AML screening of beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Draft or executed articles of association
Identification of all shareholders and beneficial owners (DBE data)
Bank KYC/AML questionnaire
Proof of corporate purpose and planned business activity
Identity documents of authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays or refuses the account, apply to another credit institution or request the Bank of France (Banque de France) to exercise the regulatory right to access a basic payment account under the Monetary and Financial Code, Article L.312-1.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An accredited legal journal (journal d'annonces légales) in the department where the registered office is located; online services facilitated via the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and publish the mandatory incorporation announcement containing the name, form (SAS), share capital, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, and legal representative(s). Retain the 'attestation de parution' issued by the journal for inclusion in the filing dossier.
required_dossiers: Text of the legal notice
Proof of payment of publication fee
Attestation of publication issued by the journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the journal rejects the notice due to statutory incompleteness, correct the text and republish; the original attestation may be voided and reissued within 24 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission of the Incorporation Dossier to the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI – Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (online portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the standard electronic form on the Guichet Unique, attach the signed articles, bank certificate, legal-notice attestation, proof of domiciliation, identity documents, declaration of beneficial owners, and the President's certificate of non-convictitness. Pay the state fee by online card. The Guichet routes the file to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, social administrations (URSSAF), and tax administration (DGFIP) simultaneously.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association (statuts)
Bank certificate of blocking of share capital
Attestation of publication in a journal d'annonces légales
Proof of registered office (lease, title, or domiciliation agreement)
Identity documents and residential address of the President
Declaration of beneficial owners (formulaire DBE)
Statement of non-conviction of the President or judicial record extract (bulletin n°3)
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet issues a 'complétude' query (incomplete file), submit the missing document within 15 days; otherwise the application is rejected with the possibility of filing a new file with incurred fees. Rapid corrective resubmission is permitted without losing priority if made within the legal time limit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the RCS Extract (Kbis), SIREN/SIRET and Automatic Administrative Affiliations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet Unique; URSSAF and DGFIP receive automatic registration data
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the greffe validates the file, the company receives an RCS number (SIREN), the Kbis extract is issued, and the company obtains SIRET, APE code (4399B or equivalent), and VAT number. Social and tax registrations (URSSAF, tax offices) are activated automatically. The blocked share capital is released following presentation of the Kbis to the bank.
required_dossiers: Guichet Unique receipt of validation
Delivered Kbis extract
SIREN and VAT number notification
Bank account release form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Kbis issuance or administrative affiliations are delayed, request a status report from the Guichet Unique; any registry oversight may be challenged before the supervising judge (juge chargé de la surveillance du registre) at the competent Tribunal de Commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Corporate Governance and Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's registered office; legal counsel or President for record keeping; appointment of statutory auditor (CAC) if statutory thresholds are reached
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the corporate records register, share register (registre des mouvements de titres), and minutes register; prepare the share certificates; hold the first shareholders' meeting acknowledging the issued shares; and appoint a statutory auditor if the company exceeds two of the three thresholds (balance sheet > EUR 4 million, turnover > EUR 8 million, employees > 50) or if the articles so require; sign the SPS coordination contract where applicable.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (Kbis)
Articles of association (final version)
Share register (registre des titres)
Minutes of the first shareholders' meeting
Managerial acceptance letters
Statutory auditor appointment letter (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the articles require a specific majority and the meeting is not validly constituted, convene an adjourned meeting with the corrected quorum; any omission in the share register is cured by rectification signed by the President.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREETS – Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (labour inspection, rope-access work authorizations) and the local Chambre de Commerce et d'Industrie (CCI) for the registration of the activity; works in existing occupied buildings fall under the coordination of the SPS Coordinator appointed by the project owner
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Déclaration d'activité pour les travaux en hauteur par techniques d'accès par cordes (rope-access operations declaration) and Carte d'Identification Professionnelle (CIP) for BTP employees, issued under the collective agreement of the Bâtiment et des Travaux Publics; the works contractor must also be registered in the RCS under APE code 4399B

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL – Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement, with the Autorité Environnementale for case-by-case screening under Article R.122-2 of the French Environment Code
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from systematic EIA for maintenance, cleaning and replacement works on existing building envelopes; however, a preliminary case-by-case examination ('examen au cas par cas') may be requested if the project modifies the structure or substantially increases the useful area; any declaration of waste handling is made under the régime de la déclaration of the ICPE if a fixed waste-processing base is established on site
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from rinsing and cleaning operations must comply with the municipal sewer discharge ordinance transposing the 21 July 2015 arrêté (pH 5.5–9.5, suspended solids and chemical thresholds); VOCs from sealants, primers and silicone adhesives must remain below the thresholds of Directive 2004/42/EC (generally 300 g/L VOC content for sealants and 100 g/L for cleaning products); glass dust and shattered glass must be collected and classified as non-hazardous construction waste (REP PMCB sorting obligations) unless contaminated
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate (avis de la Commission de sécurité) required for works affecting an ERP (établissement recevant du public); 'plan de prévention' signed with the building owner per Articles R.4512-1 et seq. of the Labour Code for multi-contractor sites; 'permis feu' issued for any hot work; structural load note approved by a certified bureau de contrôle verifying anchor points and weight capacity of the rope-access equipment; all operators must hold a professional rope-access certificate (e.g., CQP Rope Access or equivalent ISO 22846-based training) and a valid medical fitness certificate for work at height

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) for corporate income tax and VAT collection; Direction des Impôts des Non-Résidents (DINR), 10 rue du Centre, 93199 Noisy-le-Grand, France, for foreign non-established taxable persons; national tax portal: www.impots.gouv.fr. Company registration and tax identifier issuance are centralized through the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) and its 'Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises' at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. Customs export and import clearance is administered by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) through the DELTA/DEMS electronic filing platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File the standard M0 creation dossier for the SAS with the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) issues SIREN (9-digit national identifier), SIRET (14-digit establishment identifier) and the NAF/APE code aligned to ISIC 4390. Step 2: DGFiP automatically registers the entity for corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) and territorial economic contribution (CET) using the SIRET as the national tax ID; no separate TIN application is required for a resident SAS. Step 3: Obtain the French VAT intra-Community number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire, format FR + 2-digit control key + 9-digit SIREN) by filing the VAT registration form (Cerfa No. 16216 / Form 3559) with the competent SIE, normally within 15 days of the first taxable transaction. Step 4: For a foreign entity performing rope-access facade works in France without a permanent establishment, apply as a 'non-established taxable person' to the DINR using Form 3559-NR before the first taxable operation; operators established outside the EU must additionally appoint an accredited fiscal representative in France under art. 289-A of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI), while EU-established operators need no representative. Step 5: Default to the normal monthly VAT return (CA3) regime; DGFiP activates the operator's records in the EU VIES database and issues the final intra-Community VAT ID upon completion of anti-fraud screening.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: French tax law does not offer a US-style check-the-box or elective transparency regime. The SAS is statutorily classified as an entity-level taxpayer subject to corporate income tax under art. 206(1) CGI at the standard 25% headline rate and cannot elect pass-through treatment. Available statutory elections include: (i) reduced IS rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs with turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million (art. 219-II CGI); (ii) election for fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under art. 223-A CGI where a French parent holds at least 95% of the SAS, enabling single-group taxable result; (iii) option for the parent-subsidiary 'régime mère-fille' participation exemption on qualifying 5%-or-more holdings; (iv) ministerial-agreement options for global or consolidated result (bénéfice mondial/consolidé) in exceptional cases; (v) option for VAT grouping (assujettissement unique en TVA) under art. 1693-ter CGI for closely linked entities with financial, economic and organizational interconnections; (vi) option for a 3-year full or partial IS exemption as a Jeune Entreprise Innovante (JEI) where qualifying R&D expenditure thresholds are met; and (vii) the reduced taxation of dividends within the mother-daughter regime. No elective hybrid mismatch election exists: France implements ATAD (EU Directive 2016/1164) mandatorily, so hybrid payments, reverse hybrids and double-deduction mismatches are neutralized compulsorily and cannot be activated or deactivated by taxpayer election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA) — French domestic value added tax implementing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC. Ancillary territorial levies include the Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) and, until its statutory phase-out under the 2024 Finance Act, the Cotisation sur la Valeur Ajoutée des Entreprises (CVAE); these are separate territorial charges and are not invoiced as VAT surcharges.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Established suppliers benefit from the small-business exemption (franchise en base de TVA) under art. 293-B CGI: EUR 85,000 annual turnover for sales of goods and EUR 37,500 for provision of services. However, for non-established foreign suppliers the threshold is nil: any taxable supply in France triggers compulsory VAT registration from the first euro. Under art. 259-3 CGI, services relating to immovable property—including rope-access facade repair, structural glass replacement and installation works on supertall skyscrapers—are taxable in France wherever the property is located, irrespective of the supplier's establishment. Intra-Community distance sales of goods into France are taxable only above the EUR 10,000 EU-wide One-Stop-Shop (OSS) threshold, whereas construction services on French immovable property remain taxable from the first euro with no threshold relief.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing and e-reporting reform (2023 Finance Act and Décret n°2022-1299; CGI art. 289 bis): from 1 September 2026 all French-established taxable persons must be able to receive structured electronic invoices; large and mid-size enterprises must issue them from 1 September 2026, and small/micro enterprises from 1 September 2027. Invoices must flow through the national Public Invoicing Portal (Portail Public de Facturation, PPF) or a certified private dematerialization platform (PDP) using the mandatory API (API Facturation / API Partenaires) and one of the mandatory formats Factur-X 1.0, UBL 2.1 or CII 16B. Fiscal clearance is quasi real-time: transaction and payment data (e-reporting) must be transmitted to DGFiP no later than the day following invoice issuance and within 10 days of payment; the PPF serves as the central tax data hub. B2G invoices addressed to French public entities must additionally be routed via Chorus Pro with a mandatory service code. Zero-rated export invoices, although exempt with credit, remain subject to the same e-invoice and e-reporting transmission requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exonération with right to deduct) applies under art. 262-I CGI to definitive exports of goods outside the European Union evidenced by customs clearance, and under art. 262-ter CGI to qualified intra-Community dispatches evidenced by the customer's valid EU VAT identification number and transport documentation. For the rope-access facade activity, works physically performed on immovable property situated in France fall within the French place-of-supply rule under art. 259-3 CGI and are chargeable to 20% VAT; export zero-rating is not available for domestic facade operations. Zero-rating is claimable only for (i) prefabricated glass/facade modules sold and physically exported without installation, (ii) materials separately invoiced and exported for incorporation into works located outside France, and (iii) facade services executed entirely outside the EU, which are outside the scope of French VAT rather than formally zero-rated. For B2B services to foreign clients under the general art. 259-A CGI place-of-supply rule, the supplier must prove the recipient's establishment outside France and demonstrate that the supply is not connected with French immovable property; a construction contract on French skyscrapers cannot be recharacterized as an export service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DAE (Document Administratif Unique) — the customs export declaration lodged with DGDDI via the DELTA platform under Exit Code EX1 (definitive export), including the assigned MRN (Movement Reference Number) and, where applicable, the exit summary declaration (EXS) under the Union Customs Code

Commercial invoice (facture commerciale) fully compliant with art. 242-nonies A of Annexe II CGI, stating the zero-rating reference ('TVA exonérée — art. 262-I CGI') and, for intra-Community dispatches, the buyer's intra-Community VAT number
Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB) or CMR consignment note evidencing the physical removal of goods from French territory together with the applicable Incoterms

Certificate of physical exit (notification de sortie / certificat de sortie) issued by the customs office of exit, supplemented by the T5 circulation document where goods were moved in transit prior to export
Inward Remittance Certificate (bordereau de rapatriement de devises / attestation de change) issued by the paying bank evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in foreign currency

Signed completion certificate (procès-verbal de réception) and contract documentation demonstrating that facade services were de facto executed on immovable property located outside France where a zero-rated or out-of-scope treatment is claimed for offshore works
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP may claw back the full VAT incorrectly zero-rated, add statutory late-payment interest (intérêt de retard, approximately 0.2% per month), and apply the 40% bad-faith penalty (mauvaise foi), the 80% fraudulent-maneuver penalty (manœuvre frauduleuse) under art. 1729 CGI, or up to 100% in cases of organized tax fraud. Fictitious export schemes trigger the extended five-year assessment period under art. L. 186 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales (LPF) — extended to ten years where the taxpayer is established outside France or conceals its activity. Criminal sanctions under art. 1741 CGI can reach five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, aggravated to seven years and EUR 3,000,000 for organized gang fraud; art. 1737 CGI adds civil fines of up to EUR 37,500 per dishonest invoice; and the administration may suspend the taxpayer's right to invoice, block refunds, and revoke access to the e-invoicing portal. An audit file must substantiate the physical exit of goods within the statutory proof deadlines (normally three months for exports, one year for intra-Community movements) and the corresponding foreign-exchange settlement within 180 days of shipment; failure to repatriate proceeds may result in the reinvoicing and collection of French TVA on the unreported export value under the exchange-control provisions of the Code Monétaire et Financier.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting as the national central bank and foreign exchange administration within the Eurosystem; policy coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor and prudential supervision through the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution under the Code monétaire et financier, Articles L. 411-1 through L. 411-5 and R. 411-1 through R. 411-7.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France has full legal and practical convertibility for both current and capital account transactions, subject only to EU free movement of capital under TFEU Article 63 and French prudential or balance-of-payments reporting duties. There is no central bank approval requirement for inward equity subscription or outward profit remittance; no FX conversion, allocation, or surrender obligation applies to euro-denominated receipts. Dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted from an FX standpoint, provided the SAS follows French corporate distribution formalities, verifies applicable withholding tax relief under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or bilateral tax treaty, and satisfies DAC6/MDR or anti-abuse documentation requirements. Restrictions affecting capital movements exist only for strategic and defense sectors, dual-use goods, national security screening, or targeted financial sanctions imposed by the EU, UN, OFAC, and the French consolidated sanctions list.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose statutory surrender of export proceeds and does not require mandatory conversion into EUR. Export receipts from cross-border rope-access facade services may be retained in foreign currency in a dedicated currency account at an authorized credit institution without a maximum holding period. There is no minimum conversion ratio and no repatriation deadline. However, all cross-border monetary flows, including export proceeds, are subject to the Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting regime and to EU/UN sanctions screening; the reporting obligation commonly rests on the intermediary bank unless the SAS is itself designated as a declaration entity.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: CONDITIONAL/MEDIUM for operational treasury disbursements; LOW for capital escrow and statutory capital commitment. A French or EU e-money institution authorized by the ACPR or benefiting from a PSD2/E-Money Directive passport may hold safeguarded funds and execute SEPA/SWIFT payments, but it cannot receive deposits or grant credit. Digital EMIs are not acceptable as sole evidence of banking substance for the SAS capital escrow account and cannot issue documentary credits or bank guarantees; they may be used as execution-only payment rails if a Tier-1 euro settlement bank acts as the underlying treasury and clearing counterparty.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated SAS with non-resident ownership in the specialist construction services sector, major French Tier-1 banks generally require a physical KYC interview at a French branch or at the bank's prescribed international desk for the statutory Président or an expressly authorized corporate account mandataire. Remote video onboarding is legally feasible under ACPR-compliant digital identification and the French anti-money-laundering framework, but banks commonly enforce in-person attendance for non-resident UBOs and for documents requiring notarization, legalization, or apostille. The bank must independently verify the SAS legal existence in the RNE/Greffe, identify all beneficial owners, confirm the commercial substance of the facade-access business, and establish the provenance of the initial capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain runs through a non-resident intermediate holding entity with no clearly identified natural-person beneficiary in the French company register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RNE/Kbis extract from the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; certificate of registration of beneficial owners from the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs; constitutional documents of every intermediate holding entity; UBO passports and proof of residence; tax identification numbers of each entity and individual; full organizational chart showing ownership and control; management accounts; and a signed declaration of economic purpose and commercial substance for the rope-access facade construction group.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office is solely a domiciliation service with no operational premises and insufficient evidence of construction-sector substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered lease or domiciliation agreement compliant with the Code monétaire et financier; board resolution confirming the registered office; proof of operational assets such as rope-access equipment, site vehicles and safety systems; IRATA-certified technician records; health-and-safety policies; subcontractor agreements; all-risk construction and public liability insurance certificates; and SIRET/TVA intracommunautaire registration with projected payroll and worksite assignments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection or expected payment flows originate from a high-volume, non-EU jurisdiction with weak linkage to invoiced facade milestones.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve to twenty-four months of source-entity bank statements; audited or reviewed financial statements; source-of-wealth explanation letter; shareholder resolution authorizing capital subscription; executed facility and facade-replacement contracts; tender documents; purchase orders; milestone invoice schedules; project cash-flow model; and proof that payments correspond to genuine glass replacement, rope-access labor, materials procurement, and logistics costs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential undeclared subcontracting, illegal labor, or non-compliant VAT/corporate tax posture in a French construction-project context.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SIREN/SIRET registration certificate; TVA intracommunautaire certificate; URSSAF employer registration; construction-work insurance certificate; French labour-law declarations including the déclaration préalable à l'embauche; verification of subcontractor legal status and insurances; tax and social attestations; engagement letter with a French registered Expert-Comptable; and a compliance file documenting withholding tax on non-resident subcontractors where due.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and shareholder advances must be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer, with MT202 cover where interbank routing requires it, from the non-resident parent or group treasury center to the SAS IBAN at the receiving Tier-1 bank. The executing bank must map the transaction to the Banque de France balance-of-payments direct-investment category and a French motif/business-purpose code; the transfer reference must identify the share subscription, board resolution, class of shares, and advancing entity. Before value is given, the bank will verify: account purpose tag as Capital Escrow or Operational Account; current RBE/UBO records; remitter identity matching corporate resolutions; source-of-funds documentation; sanctions and embargo screening against EU/UN/OFAC and French consolidated lists; and consistency of the stated purpose with the underlying SAS corporate and construction contracts. No prior central bank FX license is required; the regime is declarative, not authorization-based.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For French and EEA counterparty payments, the treasury should use SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer cleared through T2/Eurosystem, with daily reconciliation against the SAS RIB/IBAN and VAT references. For non-EEA trade settlements, use SWIFT gpi MT103 customer credit transfers, MT202 covers where required, and irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued through SWIFT MT700/MT707 with Incoterms 2020 for facade-system materials and specialized equipment imports. Payments should be effected against presentation of compliant invoices, transport documents, insurance certificates, and completion certificates. Bank Payment Obligations under ICC URBPO 750 are permissible as a substitute for documentary LC where both counterparty banks support it. Every instruction must include beneficiary BIC/IBAN, Banque de France reporting purpose code, underlying project or contract reference, and VAT/SIRET/TVA identifier for audit traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forward contracts for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNY, and EUR/CHF exposures arising from procurement and subcontractor payments, executed under ISDA/CSA or a French market master agreement with a licensed bank counterparty
FX swaps for treasury cash-flow matching between foreign-currency receipts and euro-denominated operational outflows
Cross-currency swaps for long-term balance-sheet hedging of non-EUR intercompany shareholder loans and foreign-exchange capital exposures
Vanilla FX options, including long options and zero-premium collars, subject to bank credit approval and underlying trade or balance-sheet exposure

Non-deliverable forwards only where the underlying currency is non-convertible or restricted onshore, executed with a Banque de France-licensed credit institution or an EU/UK investment firm subject to EMIR/IFR supervision, with hedge documentation and no independent speculative trading intent

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the SAS; company records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure may lead to a court injunction and daily coercive penalty; no automatic statutory strike-off deadline applies solely for late approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts and applicable management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry through the INPI one-stop shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval; two months where filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered filing and civil fine generally of EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance; no automatic statutory strike-off timeline applies solely for non-filing, although prolonged inactivity may trigger registry removal procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the financial year-end, or by the second business day after 1 May for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest at the statutory monthly rate, and potential tax audit or assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return Form CA12, if under the simplified VAT regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the second business day after 1 May following the relevant calendar year, unless a different tax period applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest, and possible VAT assessment or penalties; not applicable to entities under the normal monthly or quarterly VAT regime.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry through the INPI one-stop shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual confirmation filing; update within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership or control information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure or inaccurate filing may result in criminal penalties for the legal representative and restrictions or sanctions affecting registry compliance; no annual strike-off rule applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory when the SAS exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at the financial year-end: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Appointment may also be required where the SAS controls or is controlled by another entity, or following a qualifying shareholder or court request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French General Accounting Plan (Plan Comptable Général). IFRS is generally relevant only where legally applicable to consolidated accounts or voluntarily adopted where permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require an annual beneficial ownership confirmation solely because a year has elapsed. The SAS must review ownership and control data annually and file an update within 30 days of any change. Share transfers must be recorded in the shareholder account records and share-transfer register, with corresponding corporate approvals and filings where required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Shareholder account records and register of shareholders
Book of shareholder and corporate decisions or minutes
Register of the President and other corporate officers
Beneficial ownership record and supporting control documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,000-10,000 per year where a statutory auditor is mandatory; otherwise 0

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) for fiscal years opening on or after 1 January 2022 (Art. 219(I)(a) CGI); 15% reduced rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable income for qualifying small enterprises with annual turnover below EUR 10,000,000 (Art. 219(I)(b) CGI).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of net taxable profit; research tax credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenses up to EUR 100,000,000 and 5% above; 3.3% social surcharge on corporate income tax where the IS due exceeds EUR 763,000 and the underlying group turnover exceeds EUR 7,630,000 (Art. 235 ter ZAA CGI); additional 3% exceptional contribution for groups with consolidated turnover above EUR 1,000,000,000 (Art. 235 ter ZCA CGI).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carry-forward without statutory time limit (Art. 209(I) CGI), subject to an annual utilisation cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding that amount; one-year carry-back (crédit d'impôt pour déficits reportés en arrière) available up to EUR 1,000,000 (Art. 220 quinquies CGI).
